Thesis and confidence
The holiday tests what voluntary membership can mean when one member's unacknowledged practical labor sustains the others' confident leisure. Iroha's wish for privacy, rest and a manageable life is intrinsically meaningful. Her anger is neither a simple failure of affection nor proof that responsibility is effortless. Makoto's dangerous vanity coexists with an actual diversion to protect Ibuki, a stated refusal to force Iroha to stay and material compensation to the boat owner. These contrary facts revise a one-note incompetence judgment without making her safe or consistently accountable.

The tournament further stages how rank, pedigree and institutional power can become play. Its victories remain dream representation. That boundary limits factual transfer without depriving the represented jokes, forced recruitment, generosity, refusals, creature affection or poetic pleasure of analytical value. Hoshino's final pleasure in seeing sea creatures supplies a positive answer distinct from the uncertain director's nihilistic account. A fantasy need not establish conquest to disclose wanted companionship and contested authority.

Confidence is high in whole local sequence, explicit statements, refused/accepted acts and dream qualification. It is qualified in reported historical explanations, the mechanics of cannon operation, the ontological status of vanished pirates, hypothetical judgments about other schools and the numerous literal actor anomalies. No consequential ambiguity required a raw-attribution expansion.

Complete episode functions and literary priorities
All27 are mandatory selected workflow scope. CORE/HIGH priorities concern literary contribution, not exclusion from coverage.

001 — HIGH, wanted invitation and an ominous preview.
The humid summer video letter is an embedded written message, not my audiovisual receiving. Makoto's claimed successful contract and luxury invitation (0011/0027) use the holiday to outshine Prefect Team training (0028–0029). Iroha questions its purpose; Ibuki adds toothbrush, swimsuit, pajamas and snacks up to300yen (0024–0025), a concrete and wanted trip. The teacher's inward acceptance (0032) is meaningful company rather than an involuntary order. The day7 drift preview (0034–0037) does not make every early happy response false; it asks how the promised experience failed.

002 — CORE, contract neglect, recipient comfort and differentiated photography.
At the boat, Makoto's signature is shown (0008); Iroha says Makoto rejected better proposals (0014), and Makoto admits the attractive low price (0015). The fisherman says confirmation photographs were sent (0021). This is not verified vendor fraud or a Prefect Team trap: Makoto's accusation is contradicted at0017. Ibuki thinks cancellation reflects her own bad behavior (0029); Makoto immediately denies that and acknowledges being wrong (0031–0032). Iroha proceeds to spare Ibuki sadness (0035). Their care is real even as boat suitability remains questionable.
The fisherman's expected Odysseia rescue (0040) is not an actual rescue guarantee; his fog/return warning (0072–0073) matters. Chiaki recounts a ghost legend, reported repeated sightings and then a social-contagion possibility (0049–0070), not independently confirmed ghosts. Iroha refuses a photograph (0082), and Chiaki dismisses it as a souvenir (0083). By contrast Chiaki asks seasick Makoto for a photo (0097), and receives assent (0098). The teacher proposes rest; Makoto accepts at0101. Iroha says a group trip is not bad (0111), then the engine actually stops (0116). Preserve the pleasure, the ignored refusal and the failure together.

003 — CORE, survival is work rather than automatic institutional status.
Communications fail (0002). Iroha's rough inspection and tank-command experience support a provisional diagnosis, not a complete engineering certification (0004–0009). Satsuki organizes inventory/spare-parts inquiry while admitting anxiety (0017–0022). Her stated trust in Makoto (0024–0025) is contrary to the teacher's skeptical alternatives.
Makoto assumes Gehenna will search for its entire leadership (0046–0051); no such effective rescue is shown. Day4 scarcity exposes that assumption. Iroha privately reveals making four portions look like five and removing desserts (0077–0084), conserving supplies without informing the others. This is useful effort and asymmetric knowledge, not transparent shared consent. She hides drifting from Ibuki to spare worry while Ibuki genuinely enjoys reported dolphins and company (0089–0096). Iroha's pleasure claim coexists with her complaint about carrying the burden (0104). The teacher offers help, while she remembers that the adult was an invited guest (0105).
Chiaki's journal, desire for readers and intolerance of repetition (0113–0117) give her writing an intrinsic aim. Fishing interrupts boredom. Her honorary club membership and promised future river (0134–0138) are not proof of practical mastery: she says this is her first actual fishing (0158). Iroha says she performs jobs in front of her without necessarily loving the school (0147–0152); this is not the absence of every relationship. They catch one small fish (0168–0173), but her “self-sufficiency” evaluation exceeds a demonstrated reliable supply. She refuses to burden the guest teacher with preparation, tries for the first time herself (0202), produces mangled sashimi and Ibuki actually eats/enjoys its novelty (0212–0216). No food-safety or nutritional adequacy outcome is established.

004 — CORE, refusal reveals the cost of unrecognized maintenance.
On day6 Makoto speculates that Hina obstructs rescue (0007–0013); the narrative does not verify that accusation. She neither knows nor cares about remaining supplies, assigning “trivial” management to Iroha (0015–0018). Crowded personal-space stress is Chiaki's explanation (0030–0033), not the sole sufficient cause of anger: dismissing work and refusing contingency matter. Iroha names the teacher and Ibuki as people put at risk (0040–0043) and apologizes for volume, not for her objection (0044).
By day7 Makoto wants water and others struggle. Iroha refuses to resume until Makoto apologizes (0065–0066). Satsuki's suggestion of hypnosis (0071) is not performed. Her skepticism that a forced formal apology would solve the matter (0075–0076) is substantive, and the others attempt fishing, eventually appealing to the teacher (0083–0087). Ibuki values Iroha's company (0092); Iroha inwardly cannot explain why release from chores and company with Ibuki are not enough (0097–0098).
Makoto refuses the suggestion to order Iroha not to leave: loyalty should be voluntary, authority should not remove free will as in “the old Gehenna” (0107–0109). Satsuki's claim that making someone believe obedience is equivalent to free will (0112) is not the account's ethics; Makoto rejects the offered method. This stated principle complicates coercive habits without erasing them. Iroha's remembered entry motive is uncertain, probably ease and status (0136–0138), not an independently fixed original history. Her wish to disappear (0145), an unknown voice (0146) and collision lead to a supposed ghost ship; causality/identity remain open.

005 — HIGH, choice, fear and protective demands.
Ibuki distinguishes a galleon from a galley (0005–0007), showing concrete knowledge. Makoto infers abandonment and proposes taking the vessel (0016/0023). Her invitation permits people to stay behind (0026–0029); it is not an order to everyone. Satsuki notices that the feared/pain-averse Makoto entered first rather than sending Iroha (0035–0039), but her mental-influence hypothesis is not proven.
Ibuki reveals she already knows about drifting and the quarrel and wants to help as a member (0042–0046); the adults' secrecy did not fully determine her knowledge. Iroha permits this subject to remaining close (0048). Satsuki dislikes solitude and accepts Ibuki's offered hand (0057–0062). Makoto admits firing at a presumed ghost (0073–0074), contradicting her earlier denial of belief. Later figures fire and surround them; Makoto directs protection and retreat (0099). The floor breaks and teacher/Satsuki/Chiaki fall (0101–0105). Their fear is not proof of an independently resolved ghost ontology.

006 — CORE, analysis and vulnerability coexist.
The separated upper group cannot reach the lower level, promises return and retreats under threat (0003–0008). That is a limited rescue ability rather than a final abandonment. Chiaki finds a lantern (0015); light helps Satsuki analyze an apparent captain's room, hierarchy, maps and tools. Her pre-Abydos-canal route, sextant and wax arguments (0047–0051) suggest an old vessel. They are in-character deductions, not an independently dated global historical reconstruction. Her ghost conclusion causes another faint, while her inference that old weapons may be ineffective (0063–0064) is still untested.
Satsuki's fear and request that Chiaki fight for her coexist with observation and organizational competence. Her “years” and experience references (0070–0075), and Chiaki's report that older members withhold earlier history (0086), do not authorize an invented former regime. Chiaki wants an article on different teacher/student perspectives (0090–0092), a genuine critical interest. Satsuki requests the teacher's hand (0100–0101), unlike a blanket unrequested-touch story. The crest-bearing handkerchief is identified as Gehenna-like (0110–0113), with pirate-student identity still queried. Makoto returns declaring herself Captain (0128).

007 — CORE, a real protective act and an incompletely witnessed leadership story.
Iroha's costume embarrassment, wall kick and request not to be sought (0005–0011) are not erased by Ibuki's matching-clothes joy and Iroha's subsequent effort (0012–0015). The one-hour flashback calls the visitors intruders (0033); Iroha's quarrel and apology to frightened Ibuki concern raised voice, not an apology to Makoto. Makoto actually draws pursuit away (0055–0057), contrary evidence against an exclusively selfish actor.
The ensuing conversion speech is Makoto's reported reconstruction (0075–0095); Iroha arrived after the followers were already organized (0105). Their obedience and pleasure at a cleaned ship (0123–0125) are represented outcomes, but the exact persuasive mechanism is not independently witnessed. Satsuki explicitly calls part of the ship explanation conjecture (0118). Makoto's looting aspiration (0144) diverts the original plan to return to land (0146). Iroha expects obsolete equipment to be harmless (0149–0150), not a tested fact. Trident's approach ends the scene.

008 — CORE, two captains' status claims produce a preventable escalation.
Sumika's captaincy was selected by lottery (0016), yet she insists on the title. She voices responsibility for safety (0035) while initially taking an impossible-looking report as hostility to her role. The010-degree/1000-yard report, absent radar signals, failed radio and ignored searchlights are printed claims (0031/0048/0057/0059), not my independent maritime measurements. She correctly observes the vessel is not necessarily hostile (0055), then hears Makoto's looting boast (0069–0070). Her personal-credit calculation (0074) leads to her actual attack order (0077); this matters when she later blames only her crew.
Internally rusted cannon and the pirates' lack of battle experience (0089–0093) contradict heroic appearance. Satsuki refuses participation (0115); Chiaki and Ibuki want to try; Iroha agrees partly to demonstrate impossibility (0117–0120). Ibuki's loading knowledge coexists with limited strength (0127–0134), and Iroha takes the heavy object. The cannon actually fires (0150–0156), overturning the local prediction. Makoto's “willpower did it” is an explanation, not an established engineering mechanism. Pirates say it has not fired since “that day” (0157); the event supplies no authorized general method of repairing cannons through belief.

009 — HIGH, demonstrated limits and authority evasion.
The first shots miss (0001). Ibuki makes an approximate ballistic table, admitting limited rifling prevents precision (0017–0020); the other crew reports improved shooting (0025). This is actual represented competence, not a new model or guarantee of hits. Sumika evades the title under threat (0033), then invokes it when caught fleeing (0036). Her crew proposes ramming with a simplistic speed-times-mass maxim (0037–0048); character rhetoric is not a physics lesson. The collision opens a hole and permits boarding (0053–0056). The role reversal exposes selective use of responsibility on both sides.

010 — CORE, apparent victory does not cure technical disadvantage.
Trident reports Makoto's strength and Sumika's initial defeat (0003), then Sumika reappears and retreats, with a self-serving claim about withholding full strength. Her vice-captain comparison (0012) is subjective. Satsuki describes trance/self-suggestion (0019–0028); it is not an independent clinical determination. Makoto's shark-feeding threats (0016/0042) are not actual executions. The crew retreats, then a main fleet arrives (0038–0040). Cannon reach and effectiveness against it remain inadequate (0043–0044), defeating a universal willpower reading.
Makoto slips; the teacher runs but cannot reach her (0047–0049); Iroha actually saves her (0050–0051). Knowledge that she cannot swim is supported by the missed-swimming-classes explanation (0056–0058), not a new medical diagnosis. The conversation about hatred/apology is interrupted. The ship actually sinks at0063. This untitled episode contains an indispensable failure and rescue endpoint.

011 — CORE, rescue, incomplete historical explanation and a limited reconciliation.
Sumika apologizes, then says she tried to stop her crew (0001–0002), contradicting her own008:0077 order. Five student passengers are reported rescued and stable (0006); the teacher is separately present, so this is not five people overall. Other passengers and even the ship are said to have vanished (0013–0015); search is ongoing (0010). No recovered bodies, confirmed deaths or verified safe passage of the pirates is supplied.
Satsuki expressly separates knowledge from conjecture (0018–0019). Her account of Gehenna's former marine-school plan, leader-named ship, launch-day sinking and ceremonial salvo (0026–0034) is reported history, with multiple causes acknowledged and the salvo described as the best-known major explanation. The similar crest belonged to that proposed school and the failed plan was erased as embarrassing history (0035–0036). It does not prove present enrollment of those figures or an exact global date. Her ghost conclusion is still bounded.
Makoto likes cherries (0044), an ordinary preference retained amid imperious service. Ibuki pushes an encounter while Iroha asks her to wait (0057–0059). Iroha questions Makoto's plan; Makoto offers contradictory confidence that she would solve it alone and that followers would inevitably come (0075–0078). She then privately admits wanting Iroha to apologize after she solved everything (0098–0099). This motive explains risk without justifying it. No mutual apology is printed. Ibuki and Chiaki interpret love (0111–0113); Iroha denies their simple reading, then herself concedes Makoto is occasionally cool (0123). That qualified appraisal is more precise than either hate or unconditional devotion.
Scene002:u0001 contains #video;11055. I received the token, not the referenced audiovisual performance.

012 — HIGH, actual hospitality and a different photographic boundary.
Odysseia supplies the luxury trip; the teacher's choice corrects Makoto's claim of having provided it (choice001). Sumika permits a false assumption that she is club head (0007–0008); this is not verified rank. The security ship is distinct from the whole academy reported returning from an expedition (0017–0019). A complete Odysseia history is not established.
Chiaki asks for a photo; security refuses ship photography (0020–0021). She clarifies a personal picture and explicitly permits refusal (0022–0025); the member assents and poses (0026–0030). This is actual differentiated recipient control, contrary to the earlier Iroha-refusal dismissal. Her treasured photograph (0031) and desire for a later interview (0037–0040) are positive without equating them to a completed interview. Satsuki acknowledges fear and seeks twice the enjoyment and company (0046–0048), not a universal contractual right to the adult.

013 — HIGH, play, an actual apology to a peer and a renewed refusal.
Ibuki assigns pirate/ninja roles to toys (0001–0004), expanding play rather than a real administrative structure. Makoto's equal-liking claim (0013), after trying to put herself first, is qualified by Iroha's observation that she forced the summary (0014). Iroha apologizes to Chiaki for making her anxious on the boat (0032–0033); this does not establish her apology to Makoto or institutional reform. Chiaki asks for the expression again for a photo (0035–0037); Iroha retracts and refuses repetition (0036/0038). No completed picture of that moment is stated.

014 — CORE, compensation supplies genuine contrary evidence.
The fisherman apologizes for maintenance (0002); Iroha acknowledges responsibility for going far despite warning (0004). A new boat is actually presented in compensation (0006–0013). Makoto distinguishes price from decades of shared value (0011–0012) and wants the best compensation. Recruitment/status rhetoric at0016 does not make that tangible gift unreal.
She admits the final naval disadvantage (0025), while enjoying the sound, movement and potential of gunfire (0028–0029). A second giant ship and Prefect-budget cut are proposed (0032–0037), not executed. Compensation does not prove safe budgeting or settled political authority. This afterstory preserves accountability and ordinary attachment without manufacturing a permanent redemption.

015 — HIGH, institutional names, misunderstood description and independent hobby.
Komori Sumika comes on a reported apology errand, treating the academy-level matter as one that “Island” could handle (0006–0007), yet wants to use the land visit for biotope/insect collecting (0011–0012). This interest is not reducible to diplomacy.
She does not know the recipient's name. A silver-haired, important, strong person's description causes a Prefect to identify Hina (0025–0029). Sumika travels to Hinomu94-13, actually meets Hina during summer training and discovers the mismatch (scene002:0013–0020). Hina is narrated as gloomy after being mistaken for Makoto (0022). This is an attribution failure, not a completed apology to the intended leader, new Hina guilt for the drifting, or a narrated collection of insects.

016 — HIGH, dreamlike drift and creature attention.
An unspecified drift-day〇 opens another sequence. Makoto renames the boat Neo Gehenna, Chiaki interviews the fish “Yona,” and Iroha calls an apparent Toramaru normal (0015–0032). These are not a verified new jurisdiction, spoken-fish biology, real tank deployment or clinical diagnoses. The later awakening bounds the whole sequence.
Ibuki notices land, initially doubted and then confirmed within the representation (0044–0055). Makoto's first-discoverer and island-name claim (0059–0060) is not global discovery history. Ibuki identifies colored hermit crabs with friends; Iroha considers food; Makoto calls one a fighter and names it Tiger Shark Maru (0063–0090). It remains represented as a hermit crab, not an actual species transformation. Naming, affection, utility and performance begin to compete.

017 — HIGH, defending dignity through an ill-explained play contest.
Abydos appears; student-number/rank claims are uttered in this dream-qualified encounter. Makoto insults the small council; Shiroko demands withdrawal (0022–0024) and clarifies that the challenge is crab fighting (0036), not a gunfight. Ibuki's objection to fighting and the clarification preserve the difference. Makoto sends Iroha because the rules are unknown to herself (0039–0041), then calls her expendable (0057), drawing an objection. Hoshino also delegates to surprised Ayane (0050–0055). No universal enlightened alternative is supplied. The crab/crayfish mismatch (0044) matters within the play's underdog plot, not an independent ecological hierarchy.

018 — HIGH, victory, ignorance and a wish not fulfilled.
The Abydos side loses; Serika corrects Hoshino's comic collapse because Ayane fought (0005). Shiroko's mind-control suspicion at0008 is unsupported, and Ayane apologizes for challenging uninformed people (0014). The rule is five collected stars (0023–0024); the Queen's “anything” ticket is reported (0026). Serika wants to pay school debt (0027); no debt is paid. Treatment for a crayfish is requested (0032–0033), not a confirmed cure. Makoto interprets encounter as providence and commits the group (0035–0040). The later dream limit applies to victory and stakes alike.

019 — HIGH, pleasure and public authority used as a challenge.
Ibuki enjoys festival smells, and Satsuki welcomes non-seafood (0004–0005). Konoka startles them, and Kanna apologizes for the manner (0007–0012). Kanna's security role and ecological-order justification (0015/0021–0022) are separate: the latter is comic rhetoric, not a newly established law of species or legitimate police intervention.
Makoto suddenly assigns Chiaki (0035–0036). Iroha enjoys watching the burden fall elsewhere, explicitly recalling her usual position (0040). Chiaki accepts given the situation (0042), showing neither a completely autonomous initial choice nor total passive inability. Her bond with Black Dory belongs in the represented play.

020 — HIGH, a limit accepted by a rival.
Konoka demands the exhausted crab rise; Kanna says not everyone is as tough and acknowledges its limit (0001–0004). She concedes defeat and hands over the star (0006–0009). They also create the conditions through which Makoto tries to convert hospitality, publicity, institutional budget power and Hina's willingness to answer for damage into domination. 1. A day off and a wanted job are different goods
001:scene001 begins with Fuuka's disbelief that SchoolLunch has a day off. Teacher's messages congratulate her and encourage doing what she wants. Shopping, a stadium, an art museum and karaoke are personally considered possibilities, not completed activities. Juri, meanwhile, chooses a waitress shift because serving lets her experience something like others enjoying her own cooking (u0023–0028). Fuuka first recommends rest, then supports that different preference. Juri wants Fuuka's rare free day protected and resolves not to call her for help (u0038–0044). Their different choices prevent equating all work with imposed burden or treating Fuuka's rest as expendable.

001:scene002 shows Juri's actual competent service: she uses the manual to propose a drink pairing, recommends a parfait she personally likes, and customers order. The manager praises her and proposes permanent work; she declines because SchoolLunch matters too (u0020–0027). This is a demonstrated ability and choice, not compensation for a supposedly worthless cook. The manager's monster rumor is initially denied; denial and embarrassment are retained. Multiple customers share the printed label ゲヘナの生徒B, so preferences do not become a single person's contradictory order.

In scene003 the chef tests a burner and collapses after an explosion; a passerby admits spilling gunpowder and asks whether cleaning was necessary. This initial accident is not Juri's cooking. The manager first presses Juri to cook despite her explicit inability, then offers to recruit Fuuka at higher pay. Juri elects to attempt the work to protect Fuuka (u0023–0057). Pressure, desire to help and her existing fear coexist; this is not unqualified freely chosen competence. In scene004 she distinguishes practice failures from serving real customers, prays for one success, and thinks the result looks promising. The final #video;10042 cue is received as text; no video content or performance has been inspected or credited.

2. Real success precedes real harm
002:scene001 Juri wants to taste before serving, but the food is taken out before that test. Customers actually call the pancake delicious and eat it; one protests the other's supposedly one-bite half-portion (u0005–0013). Juri's disbelief and pinching echo Fuuka's earlier surprise. Additional cooking and her stated happiness are actual. The later moving pancake, frightened/attacked customers and escape complicate rather than retroactively cancel the good food and wanted accomplishment. Teacher's call is incidental to their inquiry; Fuuka hears the problem and chooses to help while thanking Juri's care for her rest (u0054–0069). Her outing is interrupted, and no completed shopping/art/karaoke compensatory holiday is printed.

002:scene002 brings Iori and Chinatsu into the response. Iori's assumption that this will be trivial is an expectation, not an outcome.003 explicitly debates terrorist intent versus accident. Fuuka objects to comparison with Haruna, and the more cautious account distinguishes malicious intent from SchoolLunch's everyday feeding role (u0016–0025). Several polite explanations bear Iori's label while sounding like another participant; I preserve that seam rather than assigning them a clean voice profile. Iori leaves alone before hearing Teacher's warning, intending to protect Teacher while denying the teased concern. Chinatsu listens to Juri, jokes about interviewing her, and calls the incident accidental while admitting incomplete understanding (u0037–0056). None is a legal or hygiene audit.

Iori is found unconscious and covered in sauce. Chinatsu and Sena judge her life not endangered; Sena proposes the taste caused it, explicitly qualifying with おそらく (003:u0089–0103). This is their in-world assessment, not clinical verification. Sena appreciates Teacher's compliment on her private clothes (u0106–0108), an intrinsic ordinary pleasure within the emergency. Those are local institutional expectations, not evidence that Makoto actually intervenes here.
